alignments.note: Predicate noun of a verbless clause with the construction-supplied copula under rule 20.

The adverb is the relative clause's predicate and is recast as *in such a case*: the copula joins it under rule 20 and the supplied preposition and generic noun under rules 33 and 31, headed on *such*, which carries the lexeme.
The ASV's recasting leaves the dative preposition with no English word (rule 40).
Its suffix is likewise unrendered; the ASV writes no pronoun for it.
No conjunction morpheme opens the second colon, so the supplied connective is added under rule 14's closing sentences; the italic corroborates without deciding.
Predicate noun with the supplied copula under rule 20.
The relative particle and the resumptive possessive suffix on `אֱלֹהָיו` are carried by one *whose*, so they share a unit headed on the relative under rule 22.
The suffixed noun is the Hebrew clause's predicate and takes the construction-supplied copula under rule 20, though the ASV writes it as the English subject.

review_notes: `לּוֹ` and its suffix are unrepresented: the ASV's *in such a case* renders `כָּכָה` and writes nothing for the dative.
The copula of the last clause is placed on `אֱלֹהָיו`, read as the Hebrew predicate; the competing reading puts it on the divine name, following the English word order rather than the Hebrew clause.
